title: A Historic First for Women at the Metropolitan Opera
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, composer Missy Mazzoli discusses adapting George Saunders's Lincoln in the Bardo and becoming the first woman composer to have a world premiere at the Metropolitan Opera. Mazzoli tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini how punk helped shape her musical sensibility and why her long collaboration with librettist Royce Vavrek was essential to transforming Saunders's sprawling ghost story into an opera. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How the Iran War Is Making Alaskans Both Richer and Poorer
summary: Oil prices have surged across the United States as a result of the ongoing war in Iran. This means higher costs for households in most states, but in Alaska, the state government is bringing in new revenue from its high oil production to offset those higher costs. Some of the revenue is then redistributed to Alaskans through the state’s unique sovereign wealth fund. While most Americans disapprove of the war in Iran, Alaska may emerge as a quiet winner from one of the conflict’s most painful economic side effects: higher oil prices. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Protein Craze Fuels an Investment Boom in Livestock Health
summary: Animal health companies are tapping into the protein craze, investing billions of dollars to build up businesses focused on making cattle, pigs and poultry healthier for human consumption.

title: Berkshire Hathaway Boosts Buybacks as Operating Earnings Slide
summary: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. spent about $9.6 billion to buy back its own shares in the third quarter, a sign the company’s executives viewed the stock as undervalued. But declining insurance underwriting weighed on its operating earnings in a mixed quarter for the company.

title: Young Travelers Are Warming Up to Cruises
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News travel journalist Brittany Chang explains why cruises are attracting more Gen Z and millennial travelers as higher airfare and hotel costs make all-inclusive vacations increasingly appealing. Chang tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that cruise lines are courting younger passengers with mega ships, entertainment, adult-only spaces and nostalgia, with some sailings costing as little as about $30 a day. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Economy and Democracy Drove the Blue Wave
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Rutgers University's Ashley Koning says affordability, concerns about democracy and government corruption helped drive voters toward Democrats, with significant shifts among Latino, young and independent voters. Koning tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Democrats now face pressure to deliver tangible results on affordability before the 2028 election cycle. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Berkshire Makes Record $9.6 Billion Buyback
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Insurance Analyst Matthew Palazola breaks down Berkshire Hathaway's third-quarter results, including a record $9.6 billion in share buybacks and weaker insurance earnings. Palazola tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that CEO Greg Abel is putting Berkshire's massive cash reserves to work through buybacks, acquisitions and equity investments while maintaining the measured approach associated with Warren Buffett. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Turkey Arrests Former Regulatory Executive in Growing Fund Probe
summary: Turkish authorities arrested the former deputy chairman of the country’s markets regulator, state-run Anadolu Agency reported on Saturday, the latest executive to be caught up in a widening fund scandal.

title: Wall Street Strategists Call Stock Rout a Fresh Reason to Buy
summary: A slew of Wall Street strategists were banking on a short-term selloff following the US midterm elections to give investors an opportunity to buy stocks at a discount.

title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
summary: The guide for when to pee during movies, taking PTO to play GTA, ignoring the Foie Gras ban, and kids loving their mom and dad's music: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Jobs Surge Raises Odds of December Fed Hike
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Economics Chief US Economist Anna Wong says October's surprisingly strong jobs report showed hiring broadening into white collar, manufacturing and transportation jobs, strengthening the case for another Federal Reserve rate hike. Wong tells hosts Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo how the Bloomberg Price Project uses millions of alternative data points to provide an independent, more granular measure of US inflation. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Crypto’s Trump-Fueled Washington Boom Reaches Its Endgame
summary: Crypto’s extraordinary run of political good fortune in Washington has come to an abrupt halt. With Democrats set to control Congress following their midterm sweep, the industry faces the prospect of tougher rules and closer scrutiny of its ties to President Donald Trump.

title: Trafigura Snaps Up Copper in Asia as China Faces Supply Crunch
summary: Trafigura Group has been buying large volumes of copper to boost sales into Asia as local supplies run low, adding to a scramble for metal that’s pushed regional premiums for spot cargoes to record highs.

title: Why India’s Stock Markets Hold a Session on Diwali: Explainer
summary: India’s stock markets will open for a special shortened session on Sunday as the country celebrates Diwali, its biggest festival, keeping alive a tradition that has survived the shift from handwritten ledgers and bustling trading floors to smartphones and algorithms.

title: China Extends Gold-Buying Streak to Two Years as Prices Drop
summary: China’s central bank added to its gold reserves in October — extending a buying streak to two years — as the precious metal fell almost 7% to end the month below the $4,000-an-ounce support threshold.

title: Beijing Vows to Hit Back Against US Sanctions on China Companies
summary: China strongly opposes US sanctions on two Chinese companies over their dealings with a third party and reserves the right to take “necessary measures” to protect its interests, China’s Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday.

title: How a Bank Scandal Is Taking Down Trump’s Ally in Paraguay
summary: Officials at the Inter-American Development Bank’s investment arm suspected something was off almost as soon as they walked through the doors of Paraguay’s Ueno Bank SA.

title: The Corner Store Brings Its New York Experience to the Las Vegas Strip
summary: Catch Hospitality Group is opening a Las Vegas location of The Corner Store at the Cosmopolitan. Co-Founder and Partner Eugene Remm says the 150-seat restaurant will preserve the intimacy and authentic SoHo experience of its 75-seat New York original, rather than offer a Vegas-specific or watered-down version. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Elanco Shares Jump After Q3 Beat and Outlook Raise
summary: Elanco Animal Health shares rose nearly 8% after the company reported third-quarter earnings above expectations and raised its full-year outlook. Jeff Simmons, Elanco’s President and CEO, called it a high-quality quarter, citing 11% reported growth and broad strength across markets and product lines. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kailey Leinz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Sweetgreen CEO Says Sales Rebound After Cyclospora-Related Traffic Drop
summary: Sweetgreen CEO and Co-Founder Jonathan Neman says that sales momentum has improved after a summer Cyclospora outbreak—unrelated to Sweetgreen’s stores but damaging to traffic across the sector. The company reported October comparable sales growth of about 5%, following a return to flat comps in September, and saw further improvement in early November. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kailey Leinz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
